requirement_paraphrase: Documented operational risk framework to identify, assess, monitor, report and mitigate operational risk, embedded in enterprise risk and governance
gap_or_note: ISO ISMS covers information security risk only; CBUAE framework is wider operational risk. The ISMS has to plug into it, not stand alone
evidence_to_ask_for: Framework document; mapping of ISMS risk method to enterprise operational risk taxonomy

requirement_paraphrase: Framework covers outsourced and third-party-dependent products, processes and systems
evidence_to_ask_for: Third-party inventory linked to the operational risk register

requirement_paraphrase: Risk limits for inherent and residual exposure; appetite and tolerance explicitly address ICT, cyber and resilience risk
gap_or_note: ISO requires risk acceptance criteria, not a Board-approved appetite statement with cyber limits
evidence_to_ask_for: Risk appetite statement with ICT and cyber metrics and thresholds; Board minutes approving it

requirement_paraphrase: Internal and external fraud, including threats affecting customers, managed inside the framework
gap_or_note: ISO 27001 does not address fraud risk as such. Federal Decree-Law 6 of 2025 adds prompt reporting of fraud and security breaches
evidence_to_ask_for: Fraud risk assessment; link between fraud monitoring and SOC use cases

requirement_paraphrase: Operational resilience strategy integrated with the framework; continuous identification of threats and prompt assessment of vulnerabilities in Critical Operations
gap_or_note: ISO has continuity controls but no concept of an operational resilience strategy for Critical Operations
evidence_to_ask_for: Resilience strategy; threat intelligence intake records; vulnerability SLAs for Critical Operations assets

requirement_paraphrase: Defined triggers for Senior Management to alert the Board to actual or potential disruption
gap_or_note: ISO management review is periodic; CBUAE wants event-driven escalation
evidence_to_ask_for: Escalation criteria; examples of Board alerts

requirement_paraphrase: Each Critical Operation mapped to its people, technology, processes, data, facilities and third parties, including intragroup, with interdependencies; kept current through change management
gap_or_note: ISO asset inventory is not organised by Critical Operation and rarely captures people, facilities and intragroup dependencies together
evidence_to_ask_for: One mapping document per Critical Operation; evidence it is updated through change management

requirement_paraphrase: Minimum Critical Operations: payments and time-critical services, accurate customer and own financial records, solvency and liquidity management, plus anything the Central Bank designates
gap_or_note: Bank-specific. No equivalent in ISO 27001, NIST CSF or UAE IA
evidence_to_ask_for: List of Critical Operations with rationale; CBUAE designations if any

requirement_paraphrase: Incident response, written business continuity and disaster recovery plans for all Critical Operations
gap_or_note: Scope must be every Critical Operation, not only IT services
evidence_to_ask_for: IR plan, BCP and DR plan, each referencing the Critical Operations list

requirement_paraphrase: Board holds ultimate responsibility for the framework and must approve, oversee and ensure effectiveness of the ICT and cybersecurity risk framework
gap_or_note: ISO says top management; CBUAE says the Board, and responsibility stays with the Board even when it uses committees
evidence_to_ask_for: Board terms of reference; Board approval of the ICT and cyber framework

requirement_paraphrase: Board itself (not a committee) approves at least annually the appetite and tolerance statement, the disruption tolerance and the BCP and DR plans
gap_or_note: Stricter than ISO: named body, annual cycle, disruption tolerance has no ISO equivalent. A committee may do the annual BCP and DR review if the Board approved the initial plans and reviews them at least every three years
evidence_to_ask_for: Board minutes with dated approvals; disruption tolerance statement per Critical Operation

requirement_paraphrase: Internal audit independently reviews the operational risk framework
evidence_to_ask_for: Internal audit plan and reports covering ICT and cyber risk

requirement_paraphrase: Strong risk culture; approach communicated to staff, third parties and intragroup entities
gap_or_note: Third-party communication is often missed
evidence_to_ask_for: Awareness programme records; supplier communication of security expectations

requirement_paraphrase: Periodic stress tests including penetration testing across ICT, physical and people vectors; for Critical Functions at least, independent third-party penetration testing reported to the Board
gap_or_note: ISO does not require independent penetration testing or Board reporting of results
evidence_to_ask_for: Independent pen test reports for Critical Functions; Board paper presenting results

requirement_paraphrase: ICT and cybersecurity risk framework integrated into operational risk and resilience: identify, mitigate proportionately, monitor and test, manage proactively
evidence_to_ask_for: ISMS manual or cyber risk framework referencing the operational risk framework

requirement_paraphrase: ICT infrastructure adequate for normal and stressed conditions, protecting integrity, confidentiality and availability
evidence_to_ask_for: Capacity plans; redundancy design for Critical Operations systems

requirement_paraphrase: Board and Senior Management regularly informed of ICT and cyber exposures, incidents and weaknesses found in testing
gap_or_note: ISO management review covers this at top management level; CBUAE needs regular Board-level reporting
evidence_to_ask_for: Board cyber reporting pack and its frequency

requirement_paraphrase: Protection, detection, response and recovery programmes, regularly tested, giving situational awareness to support Critical Operations
evidence_to_ask_for: SOC use case coverage; exercise reports; detection metrics

requirement_paraphrase: Written ICT and cyber policy covering at least: governance and oversight; risk ownership; security measures (access, identity, assets, network, vendors, physical, vulnerability testing, classification); monitoring against limits; data management; operations and change and patch management; IR, BCP and DR; project management; systems acquisition and development
gap_or_note: A mature ISMS policy set usually covers this list; check project management and monitoring against limits
evidence_to_ask_for: Policy index mapped to each 8.6 item

requirement_paraphrase: Cyber risk management reviewed regularly against industry standards and emerging threats, tested against tolerance, informed by actionable intelligence
evidence_to_ask_for: Review records; threat intelligence feeding risk updates

requirement_paraphrase: Proactively manage ICT systems including those run by third parties; strategy and timeline to replace or retire obsolete or unsupported hardware and software
gap_or_note: ISO does not require an end-of-life strategy with a timeline. Unsupported software (for example PHP 7.x after php2shell, Oct 2026) needs a dated plan
evidence_to_ask_for: End-of-life register with dates; third-party system inventory

requirement_paraphrase: Master System of Record kept up to date and stored in the UAE, including when outsourced; foreign branches may keep an up-to-date UAE copy with CBUAE approval
gap_or_note: Residency is a legal requirement; ISO only reaches it through A.5.31 legal requirements. Check cloud regions and outsourced backups
evidence_to_ask_for: Data location records for the system of record; cloud region configuration; CBUAE approval if a branch

requirement_paraphrase: Comply with ICT, cyber and information security regulations from other UAE authorities
gap_or_note: This is the hook that brings UAE IA and Cyber Security Council requirements into a bank's scope
evidence_to_ask_for: Legal and regulatory register naming UAE IA and other UAE rules

requirement_paraphrase: Incident response and recovery plans for incidents that could disrupt Critical Operations, including cyber; reviewed, tested, root causes of material incidents addressed, effectiveness measured
evidence_to_ask_for: IR plan; test records; root cause reports; effectiveness metrics

requirement_paraphrase: Inventory of internal and third-party incident response resources
gap_or_note: Often missing: who your retained IR firm, forensics provider and legal counsel are, with contact paths
evidence_to_ask_for: Response resource inventory with contracts and contacts

requirement_paraphrase: Full incident lifecycle: severity classification, procedures, roles, communication including to the Central Bank, and an incident register, covering all Critical Operations
gap_or_note: Severity scheme must line up with the 15.2 and 15.3 notification triggers
evidence_to_ask_for: Severity matrix; incident register; communication templates for CBUAE

requirement_paraphrase: Data governance and protection; ICT systems support timely monitoring, loss data, and internal and external reporting including during crises
evidence_to_ask_for: Data governance policy; reporting continuity tests

requirement_paraphrase: BCP and DR for Critical Operations: scenarios from recoverable to permanent asset loss, key staff unavailability, impact analysis per scenario, activation triggers tied to maximum tolerable disruption, RTO and RPO aligned to Board tolerance, stakeholder communications including authorities
gap_or_note: ISO 27001 continuity controls are thin here; ISO 22301 is the better reference. Key staff scenarios and authority communications are common gaps
evidence_to_ask_for: BIA per Critical Operation; scenario library; RTO and RPO register; communication plan

requirement_paraphrase: Plans reviewed by second and third lines at least annually; tested at least annually for Critical Operations including key third parties, under severe but plausible scenarios; results to the Board
gap_or_note: ISO does not set an annual test cycle, third-party participation or Board reporting
evidence_to_ask_for: Test schedule and reports; evidence third parties took part; Board paper

requirement_paraphrase: Resourced change process with operational risk involved throughout; policies cover risk impact, controls, residual risk, dependency mapping, data impact, communication and emergency change; post-implementation monitoring
evidence_to_ask_for: Change policy; change records showing risk assessment and post-implementation review

requirement_paraphrase: Material changes to Critical Operations or customers: thorough testing, rollback and parallel run, independent external expert report, notify CBUAE with the report at least 30 calendar days before, written no-objection required; customers must not be harmed
gap_or_note: Regulator pre-approval and an external expert report have no ISO equivalent
evidence_to_ask_for: CBUAE submission pack; external expert report; no-objection letter

requirement_paraphrase: Board-approved third-party risk strategy; avoid over-reliance on outsourcing and keep in-house capability; risk assessment and due diligence before any arrangement
gap_or_note: Keeping in-house capability is a CBUAE test ISO does not make
evidence_to_ask_for: TPRM policy approved by the Board; due diligence files; in-house skills plan

requirement_paraphrase: For Critical Operations, verify the provider's resilience is at least equivalent; CBUAE non-objection before outsourcing that could significantly affect Critical Operations
gap_or_note: Equivalence test and regulator non-objection go beyond ISO
evidence_to_ask_for: Provider resilience assessment; CBUAE non-objection

requirement_paraphrase: Binding contracts covering rights, data ownership, confidentiality, termination and audit access; CBUAE compliance and on-site examination for critical outsourcing; same protections flow to subcontractors
gap_or_note: Check the right of CBUAE to examine on site is written in
evidence_to_ask_for: Contract clause checklist per critical supplier

requirement_paraphrase: Register of critical outsourcing, performance metrics, ongoing reporting including provider financial condition, dependency management, inclusion in BCP and mapping, viable exit plans with substitutability assessment; CBUAE may order an arrangement ended
gap_or_note: Exit plans with substitutability and financial condition monitoring are rarely in an ISO ISMS
evidence_to_ask_for: Critical outsourcing register; exit plans; supplier financial monitoring

requirement_paraphrase: Promptly notify CBUAE of significant deviations from Board-approved appetite or tolerance, or unaddressed material operational risks
gap_or_note: No ISO equivalent
evidence_to_ask_for: Notification procedure and log

requirement_paraphrase: Events that significantly affect or may affect Critical Operations: notify CBUAE within 4 hours naming the affected operations; summary report within 24 hours (event, actions, likely impact, recovery time); further notice on return to normal
gap_or_note: The clock and content are regulatory; ISO only asks you to know who to contact
evidence_to_ask_for: Runbook with 4h and 24h templates; timestamps from past events

requirement_paraphrase: Notify CBUAE within 72 hours of any high-risk incident, using Board-approved criteria
gap_or_note: Needs Board-approved criteria that line up with the severity matrix in XW-26
evidence_to_ask_for: Board-approved high-risk incident criteria

requirement_paraphrase: Policy on public disclosure of operational risk and resilience information, proportionate to size and risk
gap_or_note: Bank-specific
evidence_to_ask_for: Disclosure policy; published disclosures
